settings.goToNewDomain: We are changing the WeekToDo website to a new domain and this one will be discontinued on April 1st 2022. In order to keep your data, you must export it from this domain and then import it in the new domain (From the configuration menu). Keep in mind that if you do not migrate data, you will lose the information your browser stores in this domain. Sorry for any inconvenience this may cause.

tips.tip1: You can create a new task by clicking on any area of the list.
tips.tip2: Tasks can be dragged and dropped from one list to another, or reordered.
tips.tip3: To edit the name of a list or task, double click on it.
tips.tip4: To the right of each list's date is a snooze icon, which lets you send all pending tasks in the current list to the next day.
tips.tip5: If you don't plan on using custom lists, you can hide them in the settings menu.
tips.tip6: The calendar in the sidebar lets you quickly scroll to a date.
tips.tip7: By hovering over the name of a list, a 'mark all' icon will appear, allowing you to mark all tasks the list contains.
tips.tip8: You can create a new custom list using the 'add new list' button located on the side panel.
tips.tip9: The start button sets you on the current day.
tips.tip13: WeekToDo stores information on your computer. If you end up changing computers or browsers, remember to create a backup. You can do this in the settings menu.
tips.tip14: Click and drag the central divider to resize the calendar and custom lists. Double click it to restore its size.
tips.tip15: You can modify the number of columns and the zoom of the application in the settings panel.
tips.tip16: Click the three dots on a task to see details.
tips.tip17: You can drag and drop subtasks in the task details window.
tips.tip18: At the top of the task details window, you can change the date or task list.
